subject.title: fix: resolve Codex fork duplication when parent is unresolved (#2108)

question: Which fork-accounting implementation should become canonical: this PR's turn-identity deduplication, the parent-fingerprint approach in https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118, or a consolidated subset of both?
rationale: Both branches alter persistent cache and cross-file accounting semantics, while current main intentionally uses a conservative unresolved-parent fallback; code review alone cannot establish which identity signal is reliable across real Codex log variants.

options.title: Compare and consolidate
options.body: Run both branches against the same frozen redacted corpus, select the stable accounting model, and port only the necessary tests and fixes into one branch.

options.title: Advance this PR
options.body: Fix the two remaining cache/provenance defects and provide current-head cold and repeated warm corpus totals before choosing it over the competing branch.

options.title: Advance pull request 2118
options.body: Use the proof-positive parent-fingerprint branch as canonical and port any uniquely valuable turn-context regression coverage from this PR before closing it.

recommendation.title: Compare and consolidate
recommendation.body: Run both branches against the same frozen redacted corpus, select the stable accounting model, and port only the necessary tests and fixes into one branch.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner merged the current fallback behavior and is best positioned to select the permanent scanner contract.
